sharded_l1_investigation.outcome: NOT APPLIED (op-by-op sharding regresses; PCC fine but slower).
sharded_l1_investigation.root_cause: Per-op interleaved<->block-sharded to_memory_config conversion dominates for these tensor sizes; sharding only nets out if activations stay RESIDENT sharded across many consecutive ops (reference forward_bs: convert once, 27 SigLIP layers sharded, convert back once). Small-M expert (2 tiles) also can't divide a 2D block grid.
sharded_l1_investigation.decision: Keep validated core_grid + interleaved-L1 configs. The only viable sharded-L1 win is a full resident-sharded SigLIP encoder restructure (reference PI0_SIGLIP_BS) -- high risk/effort for ~5ms (SigLIP is only 8% of the 135ms chunk); poor ROI on a single P150. Deferred with this rationale.

resident_sharded_siglip_attempt.outcome: IMPLEMENTED, VALIDATED, MEASURED REGRESSION, REVERTED (not shipped).
resident_sharded_siglip_attempt.grid_for_11x10: (gx=9, gy=8)=72 cores (gcd(36 hidden,144 qkv,135 intermediate)=9; gy=8 divides 8 M-tiles). O-proj K padded 48->54 tiles (not div by 9).
resident_sharded_siglip_attempt.result: resident block-sharded SigLIP is ~18-22% SLOWER at batch=1; PCC fine (0.998). Reverted to interleaved baseline (diff-identical, test re-passes).
resident_sharded_siglip_attempt.root_cause: Sharding amortization needs the M dim to fill the grid. At batch=1, 256 tokens=8 M-tiles -> per_core_M=1 on the 72-core grid (severe underutilization). The per-layer BS<->interleaved reshard round-trip around SDPA (SDPA can't consume block-sharded) dominates, plus the O-proj K-pad (48->54, +12.5% FLOPs) forced by 11x10. The reference's win was tuned for batch=2/512 tokens/16 M-tiles on a 12x8 grid. The existing interleaved baseline already uses full-grid matmuls + (interleaved) LN, so the headroom isn't there at batch=1 on this device.
resident_sharded_siglip_attempt.decision: Confirms the earlier op-sweep negative result with a full resident implementation. Single-P150 batch=1 pi0.5 does not benefit from block-sharded SigLIP. Not shipped.

bfloat4_investigation.outcome: SWEPT, NOT ENABLED (default stays bfloat8_b). Available behind PI05_VLM_MLP_BF4=1.
bfloat4_investigation.decision: bf4 only helps the bandwidth-bound VLM MLP (~1.5ms / ~1% chunk) and HURTS the compute-bound expert. E2E PCC drops 0.9963->0.979 even VLM-only (prefill loss propagates via KV cache through all 10 denoise steps). For a VLA robotics policy, ~1% latency is not worth ~0.017 action-accuracy loss -- matches the reference's choice to use bf8_b (not bf4) for these weights. Default kept at bf8_b; bf4 left as an off-by-default knob.

lofi_fidelity_investigation.outcome: SWEPT, NO CHANGE. LoFi provides no benefit on this model/device.
lofi_fidelity_investigation.decision: LoFi SDPA is same-speed but lower PCC (0.9999->0.9972) -> keep HiFi2 (matches reference PI0_SDPA_HIFI=2). Matmul fidelity is within-noise across LoFi/HiFi2/default -> no change (model uses ttnn default). Root cause: at batch=1 the matmuls are bandwidth/dispatch-bound, not math-throughput-bound, so reducing fidelity frees nothing -- unlike YoloV4's compute-bound convs. No code change.

e2e_fully_traced_1cq_vs_2cq.mechanism: Composes the proven per-stage traces into ONE end-to-end replayed chunk: a single PREFIX trace (SigLIP-27 tower + mm_projector + Gemma embedding lookup + sqrt-scale + concat + 18-layer Gemma-2B VLM prefill writing the trace-safe prefix KV store) + 10 per-step static-KV denoise traces. Per-chunk eager glue is only the address-stable expert-prefix KV refill (fill_static_prefix, NO realloc, so denoise traces keep their captured buffer addresses) and the host-side Euler accumulate. NOTE: the combined embed_image+embedding+concat+forward_vlm graph captures cleanly as one trace (the earlier 'eager concat cannot consume trace-region output' limitation only applies ACROSS traces; here concat consumes an in-trace intermediate).
e2e_fully_traced_1cq_vs_2cq.two_cq: FIRST 2CQ usage in the repo (every other model pins num_command_queues=1). Device opened with num_command_queues=2; implemented as the canonical PIPELINED multi-CQ pattern (models/tt_cnn/tt/executor.py::MultiCQModelOverlappedInputExecutor + models/demos/bge_large_en performant_runner): CQ0=compute (CQ_OPS), CQ1=data-movement (CQ_IO). A STREAM of chunks is enqueued with NO per-chunk barrier and a single synchronize_device at the end; each chunk's camera uploads run on CQ1 gated by events (op_event marks 'img_bufs consumed by the prefix trace'), so chunk N+1's image upload overlaps chunk N's 10-step denoise on CQ0. Throughput is measured over a 20-chunk pipelined stream (the regime where cross-iteration input prefetch can take effect); blocking single-chunk latency is measured separately. Opens its own device (PI05_E2E_DEVICE_ID, default 1) to avoid colliding with the module-scoped `dev` fixture on device 0.
e2e_fully_traced_1cq_vs_2cq.two_cq_methodology_correction: An earlier version measured 2CQ with a per-chunk ttnn.synchronize_device inside the timing loop -- a hard barrier that drains both queues every iteration and DESTROYS the cross-iteration overlap (the '2CQ' path was serialized identically to 1CQ by construction). Fixed to the proper streaming pattern (enqueue stream -> single end sync). The corrected measurement still shows 2CQ == 1CQ, but now as a REAL result (pi0.5 is compute-bound), not a measurement artifact.

e2e_fully_traced_1cq_vs_2cq.finding: REAL 3-camera (800-token prefix) fully-traced E2E chunk = ~128.5ms on a single P150 (1.2x over eager ~156ms). Apples-to-apples vs the reference ~64.85ms/chunk (also 3-camera) -- we are ~2x off, dominated by the not-yet-ported block-sharded matmul/LN + SigLIP BS encoder perf path (analyzed/deferred above). 2CQ DOES NOT HELP, and this is now a CORRECTLY-MEASURED result (proper pipelined stream, single end-sync), not a measurement artifact: pipelined-stream throughput is 128.51ms/chunk (2CQ) vs 128.48ms/chunk (1CQ) -- identical within noise (7.78 chunks/s both). ROOT CAUSE: pi0.5 at batch=1 is overwhelmingly COMPUTE-bound. The only host I/O 2CQ can overlap is the camera upload (~3x150KB bf16 ~= 0.9MB, tens of microseconds over PCIe) hidden behind ~128ms of compute -> overlap ceiling < 0.05%. Corroborating: 1CQ streaming throughput == 1CQ blocking latency (128.48 vs 128.55ms), i.e. trace already removed host-dispatch overhead, so there is no idle bubble for a second queue to fill in the first place. 2CQ is the right tool for transfer-bound models (large/sharded DRAM inputs, e.g. the tt_cnn CNN demos it was built for); pi0.5's latency lever is the block-sharded COMPUTE path, not command queues. ACCURACY NOTE: trace FIDELITY stays excellent (traced-vs-eager 0.997-0.999), but TTNN-vs-torch E2E action PCC scales DOWN with prefix length: 0.998 at 1 camera (288 tok) -> ~0.982-0.985 at 3 cameras (800 tok).
